app.name: Base
app.one_liner: A Mac-first workspace orchestrator that standardizes developer environment setup, shell initialization, and command execution across multiple peer project repositories.

screens.name: Workspace Dashboard
screens.purpose: Display discovered project repositories and provide access to unified workspace actions like setup, validation, and testing.

rust_commands.name: basectl_check
rust_commands.purpose: Validate the current workspace state and report any inconsistencies or missing dependencies.

rust_commands.name: basectl_doctor
rust_commands.purpose: Diagnose common workspace setup and configuration issues.

rust_commands.name: basectl_projects_list
rust_commands.purpose: Discover and list all participating project repositories adjacent to Base under a shared parent directory.

rust_commands.name: basectl_setup
rust_commands.purpose: Bootstrap the entire workspace or a specific project repository using standardized conventions.

rust_commands.name: basectl_test
rust_commands.purpose: Execute standardized tests across the workspace or a specific project.

mvp_plan: week 1: Build core `basectl` CLI with setup, check, and list commands
week 1: Create basic workspace validation routines
week 1: Implement project discovery logic based on shared parent directory layout
week 2: Add support for project-specific setup via conventions or manifests
week 2: Implement test orchestration across discovered projects
week 2: Integrate shell environment bootstrap via `base_init.sh`
acceptance_tests: Given a Base repo and two project repos checked out side-by-side under a common parent, when the user runs `basectl projects list`, then both project names are returned.
When the user runs `basectl check`, then the system validates that all required tools and conventions are present and reports any missing components.
When the user runs `basectl setup`, then a consistent shell environment is initialized and shared libraries are made available across all discovered projects.
